title: Review: Exothermic and endothermic reactions; Chemical cells and fuel cells (chemistry only)
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.5.2-c05, 4.5.1-c15, 4.5.2-c06, 4.5.1-c17. Clues: 4.5.2-c05 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.5.1-c15 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.2-c06 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.5.1-c17 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.2-q08, 4.5.2-q09, 4.5.2-q17, 4.5.1-q19, 4.5.2-q02, 4.5.2-q11, 4.5.1-q20, 4.5.2-q04, 4.5.2-q13, 4.5.1-q16, 4.5.2-q07, 4.5.2-q10, 4.5.1-q28. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Simple cell
items.clue: Two different metals in contact with a conducting solution.

items.label: Activation energy
items.clue: The minimum amount of energy that particles must have to react.

items.label: Battery
items.clue: Two or more cells connected together to give a greater voltage.

items.label: Overall energy change
items.clue: The difference in energy between the reactants and the products, shown on a reaction profile and, at higher tier, calculated from bond energies.

questions.stem: A rechargeable cell is connected to an external electrical supply. What happens inside the cell?

options.text: The chemical reactions are reversed
Fresh reactants are pushed into the cell
Extra electrons are stored inside it
The used-up reactants are all removed

questions.explanation: Rechargeable cells can be recharged because the chemical reactions are reversed when an external current is supplied.

questions.stem: Cells are made from a copper electrode and one other metal in the same electrolyte. The voltages are: magnesium 2.7 V, zinc 1.1 V, iron 0.8 V. Tin is less reactive than iron but more reactive than copper. What voltage would a tin and copper cell most likely give?

options.text: About 1.9 V, from the zinc and iron values added
About 3.4 V, since tin is the least reactive metal
About 0.5 V, because tin is close to copper in reactivity
About 2.7 V, the same as the magnesium cell gives

questions.stem: A games controller is used every day and flattens its cells within a week. Which is the best reason for choosing rechargeable cells for it?

options.text: They can be reused many times, so fewer cells are bought
Recharging pushes new chemicals in, so they never wear out
They hold much more electricity inside them when new
They cost less to buy than an alkaline cell does

questions.explanation: With heavy daily use the cost and waste of replacing cells each week outweigh the higher purchase price of a rechargeable cell.

questions.stem: A student draws a reaction profile for an endothermic reaction. Which description of the drawing is correct?

options.text: The products line lies below the reactants, joined by a curve with a peak.
A straight sloping line runs from the reactants line up to the products.
The products line lies above the reactants, joined by a curved peak.
The top of the curve is level with the products line on the right.

questions.explanation: Endothermic products are higher in energy than the reactants, and the specification asks for a curved line passing over the activation energy peak.

questions.stem: Two cells are identical except that one uses zinc and copper electrodes and the other uses magnesium and copper. The cells give different voltages. Why?

options.text: The voltage depends on how much electrolyte there is
The voltage depends on the type of electrode used
The voltage depends on the area of the electrode
The voltage depends on the wire joining them up

questions.explanation: The voltage produced by a cell depends on a number of factors, including the type of electrode.

questions.stem: In a hydrogen fuel cell, how does the fuel produce a potential difference?

options.text: It is oxidised electrochemically at an electrode
It is burned, and the heat drives a generator
It is reduced by oxygen at the negative electrode
It is decomposed by a current supplied to the cell

questions.explanation: The fuel is oxidised electrochemically within the fuel cell to produce a potential difference.

questions.stem: A reaction profile shows the products at a lower energy than the reactants. What does this tell you about the reaction?

options.text: It is endothermic and takes in energy overall.
It is exothermic only if the peak is low.
It cannot happen, as products must be higher.
It is exothermic and gives out energy.

questions.explanation: Products lower than reactants means the chemicals have lost energy, and that energy has gone to the surroundings.

questions.stem: Which pair of electrodes, dipped into an electrolyte, would produce a voltage?

options.text: Two identical strips of copper metal
Two copper strips of different size
Two carbon rods taken from cells
A zinc strip and a copper strip

questions.explanation: A simple cell is made by connecting two different metals in contact with an electrolyte.

questions.stem: Why are hydrogen fuel cells described as a potential alternative to rechargeable cells and batteries?

options.text: They can be refilled with electricity at any charge point
They store far more electricity inside them than a battery
They need no fuel or oxygen once they have been started
They keep working while hydrogen is supplied, with no recharging

questions.explanation: A fuel cell runs on an external fuel supply, so it does not have to be taken out of use to recharge.

questions.stem: Two reactant particles collide with each other but no reaction takes place. What is the reason?

options.text: Every collision must react, so this cannot happen.
They collided with less than the energy given out here.
They collided with too little energy to react.
The reaction is exothermic, so no energy is needed.

questions.explanation: Reactions occur only when particles collide with sufficient energy; a collision below the activation energy simply bounces apart.

questions.stem: Which statement about alkaline batteries is correct?

options.text: They can be recharged from the mains many times over
They are rechargeable once the alkali is replaced
They work again once fresh reactants are added
They are non-rechargeable, so they are replaced

questions.explanation: The specification states that alkaline batteries are non-rechargeable.

questions.stem: Where does the hydrogen in a hydrogen fuel cell come from?

options.text: It is stored inside the cell when the cell is built
It is made inside the cell from air and water
It is released by the electrolyte as it runs
It is fed in from an external supply of the fuel

questions.explanation: Fuel cells are supplied by an external source of fuel (eg hydrogen) and oxygen or air.

questions.stem: A reaction is endothermic. What does this tell you about the bond energy sums?

options.text: More bonds are broken than are formed in this reaction.
Breaking bonds needs more than forming lets out.
Forming bonds gives out more than breaking needs.
Forming new bonds takes in energy, making it endothermic.

questions.explanation: The specification states that in an endothermic reaction the energy needed to break existing bonds is greater than the energy released from forming new bonds.
